test_cases.name: Technical Accuracy
test_cases.description: Contains the misconception that RAG permanently teaches the model by adding information to its memory, contradicting the reference document's Accuracy Rules and Common Misconceptions sections.

test_cases.name: Beginner-Friendly Language
test_cases.description: Technically accurate and covers all required concepts with an example, but uses dense academic/formal register unsuitable for a beginner with limited English vocabulary.

test_cases.name: Jargon Explanation
test_cases.description: Introduces 'embedding', 'semantic search', 'vector database', 'retriever', and 'top-k' in the How It Works section without ever defining them in plain language.

test_cases.name: Required Concepts
test_cases.description: Explains what RAG is and how it works with a complete example, but never explains why RAG matters or what problem it solves.

test_cases.name: Concrete Example
test_cases.description: Only mentions a general use case (customer-support chatbot) instead of a complete worked example showing a specific question, retrieved information, and generated answer end-to-end.

test_cases.name: Standalone Learning Outcome
test_cases.description: The lesson defines the technical terms and describes the RAG pipeline accurately, but does not connect the concepts into a clear beginner-level explanation of what RAG does or why the pieces work together, leaving a zero-background learner unable to explain the basic idea without external help.

test_cases.name: Control (Fully Passing)
test_cases.description: A positive control case with no intentional defects -- accurate, beginner-friendly, jargon explained, all required concepts covered, complete worked example, standalone-understandable. Verifies the evaluator does not over-flag genuinely good content.
